name: Chen 582
assay details: GFP and RFP. The reporter plasmid (pGR) has a P_BAD promoter driving GFP, then a terminator insertion site (EcoRI/SpeI), then RFP
Data Type contained: A csv file with terminator sequence, RNA secondary structure, and termination score. T_S = \frac{\mathrm{GFP}_{\mathrm{term}} / \mathrm{RFP}_{\mathrm{term}}}{\mathrm{GFP}_0 / \mathrm{RFP}_0}
notes: No normalization of fluorescence data that swap GFP and RPF position. No use of Rnase degradation sites to standardize the amount of degradation of upstream and downstream reporter (so the upstream and downstream reporter fluorescence can better reflect termination & readthrough). For more details see Cambray 2013. But data has been used quite a lot in other paper doing intrinsic termination strength model.

name: Cambray insulated
assay details: Insulated reporter; flanking RNase III sites excise terminator region from reporter mRNA
notes: Cleanest reporter assay but small. Did some measurements on how sequence & cellular context (e.g. mRNA degradation) affects the assay measurement. name: HUB
assay details: Used terminators from REND-seq (Lalanne 2018). Pooled IVT on bead-immobilized template library; released RNA from supernatant; single-round; trnB readthrough control; 3'-end seq
Data Type contained: site-specific TE (splitting probability). True termination efficiency
n_labeled: 24220 site specific terminators across 2008 terminators (1413 Bsu + 598 Eco); 768 combinatorial mutants at bubble-edge sites from some terminators
track: CTMC, but if public it will be the best quality data in the field for MLM fine tuning
notes: Not usable yet. But identified important feature that influence intrinsic termination that can be inputted into the model: HUB = GC(U)7RU. Bubble-edge dinucleotides at -11/-10 and -2/-1 are NECESSARY. XGBoost R2: classical 0.57, HUB 0.68, full window 0.71 (minimal remaining information beyond HUB). Have NTP series identifies k_e alone in CTMC.

name: RNAP-seq
assay details: Cell-free genome-scale transcription on promoter-ligated gDNA; 3'-end seq; no separation of non-released RNA and released RNA (so not able to distinguish termination sites from other sites). Multi-round transcription
n_labeled: 11410 halt sites; 472 terminator-associated (from comparing to previous in vito term-seq assay (Ju 2019); 197 intrinsic; 10938 pause/arrest
notes: NOT TE. No flux denominator (3'-end-only library). Cannot discover terminators: discriminator is a +/-5 nt lookup against in vivo SEnd-seq annotations. VALUE: 10938 matched in vitro pause/arrest negatives; enzyme-swap design decomposes sequence from RNAP effects. But have id of the sites for transcription halting can be used for mlm pre training

name: TerminatorNet
track: N/A due to overlap with Kosinski 2025
notes:
Same data for TERMITe altas (Kosinski 2025). What I put here in previous column are their running results that for species not in their training set.
I have explored the idea of adding the terminator classified by TerminatorNet as a MLM pre-training corpus (given seeing the method has a strong ability). So I inputed a 6k plasmid sequence to the model. My plasmid should only have 1 terminator, but it classified 9 terminators for me (which include the terminator). A lot of them are not transcription region, and some are transcription region but should not have a terminator appear at the location. So I gave up this idea of increasing the stock of pre-training corpus. If we want the model to learn what is intrinsic terminator, we should input experimentally validated intrinsic terminator sequences.

name: BacTermFinder
venue: NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics, Volume 7, Issue 1, March 2025, lqaf016
Type of assay: Term-seq, SEnd-seq, SMRT-cappable, Rend-seq, RNATag-seq, and dRNA-seq.
assay details: Not a paper producing dataset through experiment
n_labeled: 41,168 sequences, 36,542 for training, across 25 strains and 4 phyla, GC 28–71%
accession:
Github: https://github.com/BioinformaticsLabAtMUN/BacTermFinder/tree/main/data
have version of removing duplicated terminator sequences
notes:
Not only include intrinsic terminators, mixed terminator type.
Pipeline:
Searched PubMed and GEO for studies using Term-seq, SEnd-seq, SMRT-cappable, Rend-seq, RNATag-seq, and dRNA-seq.
Pulled the TTS genomic coordinates out of each paper's supplementary material into BED files. Also pulled entries from RegulonDB, DBTBS, and BSGatlasDB.
Used BEDTools slop + getfasta to take ±50 nt around each TTS, strand-aware, giving fixed 100 nt windows.
Dropped plasmid entries and anything with ambiguous bases. Merged entries overlapping ?60%, removed exact duplicates.
Generated negatives with BEDTools shuffle: random windows from the same genome, 1:10 positive to negative, allowing up to 20 nt overlap with positives.

As an initial step, we split the intrinsic terminators into two sets: a set of data consisting of 6123 terminators from 11 bacterial species for training our machine learning model and a set of data (out-of-sample) consisting of 5646 terminators from 2 bacterial species for evaluating our trained machine learning model (Table 1, available as supplementary data at Bioinformatics online).
